chunks: Contentment is a capital that does not dwindle. He who remembers death much is satisfied with small favours in this world. He who knows that his speech is also a part of his action speaks less except where he has some purpose.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life or temporal existence
key_terms.ذِكْر الْمَوْت: Remembrance of death, a practice to reduce attachment to the world
key_terms.قَنَاعَة: Contentment or sufficiency, a state of being pleased with what one has

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of remembering death and practicing contentment in Islam?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha, this maxim encapsulates the Shia ethical ideal of *zuhd* (asceticism) by redefining wealth as inner contentment rather than material accumulation. The linkage of speech to action reflects the concept of *amal* encompassing both physical deeds and verbal conduct, while frequent remembrance of death (*dhikr al-mawt*) serves as a practical mechanism to detach the heart from worldly distractions.
